### We’re proud to announce the first public release of WinNative

WinNative is a modern, open source Winlator fork built for the experience we wanted ourselves. It started as something we wanted to use, and now we’re excited to share it with the community.

### Notable features:

- Modern Jetpack Compose UI replacing Winlator’s legacy XML interface.
- Built for long play sessions, with controls and audio designed to remain stable during 8+ hour sessions.
- Easy to follow setup wizard for users who are new to Winlator.
- Basic Steam, Epic Games, and GOG integrations for personal game library support.
- Google Play support for secure login token saving and restoration.
- Built in component and driver fetcher with GitHub integration.
- Noticeable performance improvements compared to GameHub and similar apps.

### Other notes:
- This is a 0.1.0 release, so bugs are expected and already being tracked. WinNative will continue to improve over the next several releases, with more polish, fixes, and expanded features coming over time.

## BannerHub Lite v1.0.2

Adds the BannerHub AI Frame Generation menu to BHL, plus fixes the firmware-on-first-game-add path so the URGENT warning from v1.0.1 should no longer be needed.

> 🆕 **Firmware fix is server-side.** The "Failed to initialize the simulator" / "firmware still on 1.3.3" issue from v1.0.1 was a stale row in the BannerHub API's `executeScript` endpoint — the Add-Game path was advertising the old `imagefs.zst` (1.3.3) even though the upgrade-check endpoint was on 1.3.7. releases.name: BannerHub Lite v0.3.7-pre3
releases.body:
**fix: Winlator HUD FPS reading**

In Lite 5.1.4, `WineActivity.j` is a Map — not an IHudDataProvider — so `readFps()` silently returned 0.

Fix: `BhFrameRating.readFps()` now reads from `WineActivity.i` (HUDUpdater) → `g()F`, which is the same averaged frame-list source the native HUD uses. Falls back to the original `j` path for BH 5.3.5 base APKs.

releases.body:
Fix: Winlator HUD toggle injection

Changes in this build:
- **HUD injection fix**: Fragment context IS WineActivity — no longer uses fragile WineActivity.t1 reflection; cast ctx directly to Activity
- **ContentView target**: HUD now added to android.R.id.content + bringToFront() to ensure it renders above Wine surface
- **Verbose logging**: every step in the HUD toggle path logs to BannerHub tag for debugging

To test: open a game in Wine, open the Controls sidebar, toggle 'Winlator HUD'. The HUD overlay should appear in the top-right corner.

- **Problem:** When entering some cities, the game would crash and close.
- **Fix:** Problem fixed, and you can now teleport and enter cities perfectly.

### 🐛 Bug: Monsters ignored the CLIENT when the HOST was far away
- **Problem:** Monsters only attacked when the HOST was nearby. If only the CLIENT approached, the monster would remain still.
- **Fix:** Detection now compares the HOST and all CLIENTs present on the same map and returns the **closest** to the monster as the target.

- **Problem:** Monsters scaled based on 0+ (extra players). × 2), resulting in level 2 Goblins in a session with 2

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.2.0
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.2.0

### New
- **Lemon FG, Lemon's own frame generation.** Built in, nothing to install, and no Lossless Scaling code in it: turn it on in Settings → Graphics → Frame generation, for all games or one. A new **Engine** option picks Lemon FG (default) or Lossless Scaling, which only runs with your own copy of `Lossless.dll`. The FPS counter shows which one is working, and Lemon FG has its own lemon icon. The setup screen explains that Lemon FG is included instead of only offering to load the DLL.
- **Accurate is the default GPU mode again** in Lemon: the optimizations in this version pay for most of its cost (measured: TOTK 48.1 → 47.9 fps on an AYN Odin 3, BOTW 16.6 → 17.0 fps on a Galaxy S24 Ultra). Lemon Lite and Lemon Lite & Spoofed keep Fast.
- **One lighter wait for the GPU.** Lemon still waits for the GPU before a game reuses what was drawn, so the flickering fixed in 1.1 stays fixed, but it no longer drains the GPU when the game waits for work that is already queued (Garfield: GPU thread stalls from ~156 to ~13 ms per second). The GPU Fence Behavior option is gone: there is nothing to set.
- **Mali GPUs**: BC4 and BC5 textures are recompressed to EAC on th

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.1.0
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.1.0

### Three builds
- **Lemon**: the full version, as before.
- **Lemon Lite**: lighter defaults for weaker GPUs (0.75x resolution, asynchronous shaders on), without the bundled Lemon-Ade driver, and experimental PanVK drivers for Mali-G720 and Mali-G52 in the driver downloader (each GPU only sees its own). It installs next to Lemon and can import your keys, firmware, games and saves from it.
- **Lemon Lite & Spoofed**: Lite under another package name, so phones that boost known benchmark apps may run it faster. Experimental: it depends on the phone.

### New
- **Online play on Nextendo Network** (Settings → Online). Sign in from the browser and play online; Mario Kart 8 Deluxe races work.
- **Settings in ten categories** (Lemon, Graphics, Performance, Controls, In-game display, Console, Online, Content and data, Help, Advanced and debugging), and **a search** on the settings home that finds any option, however deep it is, and takes you straight to it.
- **No more flickering in Fast GPU mode** (Garfield - Escape From Monday, Dragon Ball and others): the game now waits for the GPU before it reuses what was drawn. That makes **Fast the default GPU mode again**,

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.0.1
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.0.1

### New
- **Quick Load survives dying.** Save, die (or move on in the game), load: you are back where you saved. A load now undoes what the game changed since the save outside its own memory (GPU buffers and mappings, thread stacks, open files and other service objects, worker threads destroyed and created again) before rewinding. It also no longer fails now and then when a service answered in the middle of a load. Still experimental: if a game did something it cannot undo yet, the load tells you and changes nothing. The state is only kept while the app stays open.
- **Grid and list views** for big libraries, next to the carousel.
- **Library scan progress**: a bar while your games are read, including the one-time decompression of a solid `.nsz` (which used to look like an empty library for minutes), and pull down to refresh.
- **Start in QLaunch** (Settings → App Settings, under Buttons): with the firmware installed, opening Lemon boots straight into the console's home menu. Thanks to the user who asked for it.
- A tap on the game closes the in-game menu.
- **Enable Legacy Rescale Pass** is now listed under Settings → Graphics → Hacks. It fixes the colored

releases.name: Lemon v0.3.4
releases.body:
## Lemon v0.3.4

Hotfix for v0.3.3.

### Fixes

- **The loading screen could stay up forever after a game had started.** The check that hides it once the game shows its first frame could get cancelled, most often by touching the screen while the game was loading, and it was never restarted. It now runs independently of the touch controls, so the loading screen always goes away as soon as the game is on screen.
- The adaptive performance watchdog (automatic downgrade when a game can't keep up) had the same problem and could silently stop working; fixed as well.

See the [README changelog](https://github.com/Ghael-V/Lemon-Project#changelog) for the full history.

releases.name: Lemon v0.3.3
releases.body:
## Lemon v0.3.3

Compressed game dumps, a round of rendering and crash fixes, and a more robust game list. Includes everything from v0.3.2-nightly.1.

### New

- **`.nsz` and `.xcz` support.** Compressed dumps load straight from your games folder, no need to decompress them first.
  - Block-compressed files (the `.xcz` default, or `nsz -B`) are read in place: only the parts the game asks for are decompressed, and nothing is written to disk.
  - Solid `.nsz` files can't be read in place, so they're decompressed once on first use and cached for later launches. The cache is capped at 24 GiB; the least recently used games are evicted first.

### Fixes

- **Rendering:** added a missing barrier before indirect compute dispatches, compute dispatches are never skipped anymore, and fixed crashes on dead compute descriptor slots and when rescaling texel buffer views.
- **Pipeline cache:** a corrupted or truncated cache is now rejected instead of crashing the game on launch.
- **Loading screen** stays up until the first real frame is rendered.
- **Older Adreno devices (Snapdragon 888/865):** the custom GPU driver is no longer loaded and unloaded repeatedly, which could crash importing or usin

releases.name: Lemon v0.3.2-nightly.1
releases.body:
Prerelease build for testing - not a stable release.

### Fixes

- **Quick Save/Quick Load could abort mid-restore on a legitimate, non-corrupt savestate.** `Restore()` treated any partially-unmapped memory region as fatal file corruption and bailed out - leaving memory half-reverted and thread contexts completely untouched. Confirmed via a real device log that a region can legitimately become partially unmapped between capture and restore (e.g. a heap allocation the guest freed in between) with no corruption involved. Now that region is skipped, the same way an excluded sleeping-thread stack already is, and the restore continues instead of aborting.
- Fixed a crash on some older Adreno/KGSL devices (confirmed on Snapdragon 888 and Snapdragon 865) when importing a custom GPU driver (e.g. Turnip) from your own file in the driver manager, instead of the in-app downloader. The driver manager's info labels (`getSystemDriverInfo()`/`getGpuModel()`) were each building a full renderer-grade Vulkan device just to read two strings for the UI, and that churn - two full probes back-to-back plus a real driver reload - stacked into several rapid open/close cycles of the GPU driver library, a kn

releases.name: Lemon v0.3.1
releases.body:
## Lemon v0.3.1

Patch release fixing the auto-updater and cleaning up remaining "Eden" branding.

### Fixes

- **The auto-updater never actually ran.** `enable_update_checks` defaulted to `false`, so the update check never fired for anyone who hadn't manually found and flipped a Settings toggle they had no reason to know existed. Now on by default (still user-toggleable in Settings).
- A separate tag-comparison bug in the update checker (inherited from upstream, written for a two-segment `MAJOR.MINOR` tag scheme) meant Nightly-flavored builds' comparison always bailed out silently even after the setting was fixed. Fixed.
- Remaining "Eden" leftovers renamed to "Lemon": the device/system nickname shown in Settings > Advanced (reported by a user), plus a few lower-visibility internal identifiers (audio session name, SDL app-name hint, GPU crash-dump description, WebService default username).

See the [README changelog](https://github.com/Ghael-V/Lemon-Project#changelog) for the full history.

releases.name: Lemon v0.3
releases.body:
## Lemon v0.3

**Nightly and Experimental are merged into `main` and retired as separate channels as of this release** — one consolidated build going forward.

### Highlights

- **Savestate reliability**: Quick Save/Quick Load now excludes threads asleep on a kernel wait from the restore instead of corrupting their stack/context, making it reliable on real multi-threaded games (previously same-session only, MVP-quality). Savestate files also shrunk ~3x via sparse-encoding zero-filled memory pages.
- **Rendering fix**: a missing Vulkan synchronization barrier between compute-shader dispatches and the draws/copies that consume their output caused intermittent black rendering artifacts (confirmed on Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom's procedural grass and shadows).
- **Crash fixes**: retry custom GPU driver loading instead of falling back to the system driver after a single attempt (fixes a repeated crash-on-launch pattern confirmed on Snapdragon 888/Adreno 660); fixed a native out-of-bounds memory-unmap during shutdown that could corrupt state carried into the next game session; fixed a crash opening Settings after exiting emulation.
- **Build system**: Release builds were silently sharing

releases.body:
Build experimental (applicationId propio, `dev.lemon.lemon_emulator.experimental`). **No es un release estable** - prerelease.

## Posible fix de los cierres al arrancar en Snapdragon 888

Un tester con Snapdragon 888 (Adreno 660) nos pasó logs reales del crash. Rastreando el problema encontramos que, al abrir la pantalla de emulación, dos funciones de diagnóstico (usadas solo para mostrar info del driver en el gestor de drivers - no las usa el renderizador real del juego) creaban un dispositivo Vulkan completo contra el **driver del sistema**, sin ningún `try/catch` - a diferencia de otras funciones similares del propio código que sí lo tienen. En ese dispositivo concreto, el driver del sistema reporta especificaciones incompletas (`maxViewports=1` en vez de 16+, sin soporte de `multiViewport`), y la creación del dispositivo puede fallar de forma no capturada, tirando la app entera abajo antes de que el juego llegue a arrancar - aunque el renderizador real habría usado el driver personalizado (Turnip) sin problema.

Añadido el mismo manejo de excepciones que ya usan las funciones equivalentes vecinas.

**Importante:** no podemos confirmarlo al 100% sin ese hardware concreto - si e

releases.name: Lemon Experimental v0.2.6 — Fix hierba/sombras negras en TOTK
releases.body:
Build experimental (applicationId propio, `dev.lemon.lemon_emulator.experimental`, convive en el mismo dispositivo con la build estándar y la nightly). **No es un release estable** - prerelease.

## Fallo corregido: hierba/cajas negras en Zelda TOTK

En Tears of the Kingdom, la hierba procedural (y en ocasiones las sombras) se renderizaba como cajas negras sólidas que aparecían y desaparecían aleatoriamente al mover la cámara.

**Causa raíz:** faltaba una barrera de sincronización Vulkan entre el compute shader que genera/posiciona la hierba y el draw que la pinta. Un draw podía leer el buffer que ese compute shader todavía no había terminado de escribir - una carrera dependiente del hardware que no deja rastro en los logs. Rastreando el código del `buffer_cache`: no había ningún mecanismo que protegiera esa dependencia, la añado.

Verificado en dispositivo en TOTK: **mejora estimada del 80-90%**.

## Otro arreglo: posible causa de cierres al arrancar en Snapdragon 888

Se reportaron cierres repetidos justo al abrir la app en un dispositivo Snapdragon 888 (Adreno 660), sin ANR y sin logs. La carga del driver Vulkan personalizado (`adrenotools`) se disparaba en cada arranque de la a

releases.name: Lemon Nightly v0.2.5 — Paridad total con Experimental
releases.body:
Build Nightly (applicationId propio, `dev.lemon.lemon_emulator.nightly`, convive en el mismo dispositivo con la build estándar y la experimental). **No es un release estable** - se publica como prerelease.

Tras varios días sin reportes de fallos en la build experimental (~75 descargas), Nightly pasa a tener **las mismas features que Experimental** - ya no hay diferencia entre ambos canales.

## Novedades

- **Quick Save / Quick Load** - savestate funcional en juegos reales multi-hilo (ver notas de los releases experimentales anteriores para el detalle técnico). Sigue sin ser 100% infalible en todos los juegos/momentos, pero funciona la gran mayoría de las veces con fallo controlado cuando no.
- **Sombreadores de cómputo asíncronos** - la opción "Usar sombreadores asíncronos" ahora también cubre los pipelines de cómputo (antes solo gráficos), reduciendo tirones en juegos que usan mucho compute shader (partículas, culling...).
- **Diseño del mando** - nueva entrada en el menú de pausa con 3 presets (por defecto, botones grandes, cruceta/stick intercambiados) y acceso directo a "Editar superposición". Aplicar un preset o entrar en edición ahora muestra el mando automáticamente si est

releases.name: Lemon Experimental v0.2.4.2 — Savestates ~3x más pequeños
releases.body:
Build experimental (applicationId propio, \`dev.lemon.lemon_emulator.experimental\`, convive en el mismo dispositivo con la build estándar). **No es un release estable** - prerelease, no interfiere con el comprobador de actualizaciones de la build normal.

## Novedad sobre [v0.2.4-experimental.1](https://github.com/Ghael-V/Lemon-Project/releases/tag/v0.2.4-experimental.1): savestates mucho más pequeños y rápidos

El fichero de Quick Save era un volcado completo sin comprimir de toda la memoria activa del juego - varios GB por guardado. Medido en un juego real (Super Mario 3D World): ~80% de esos bytes eran directamente cero (memoria reservada que el juego nunca llega a tocar).

- El guardado ahora detecta y salta bloques de 4K completamente a cero (solo un `memcmp`, sin compresión real de por medio) en vez de escribirlos.
- Verificado en dispositivo: un savestate de 3.429.812.272 bytes pasa a 1.078.708.062 bytes - **reducción del 68,6%**, casi exacto a lo medido de antemano.
- Quick Save también es visiblemente más rápido al escribir ~3x menos datos a disco.

No cambia nada de la lógica que evita el crash (exclusión de hilos dormidos, reintento antes de cargar) - sigue igual que en

releases.name: Lemon Experimental v0.2.4 — Savestate funcional (beta)
releases.body:
Build experimental (applicationId propio, `dev.lemon.lemon_emulator.experimental`, convive en el mismo dispositivo con la build estándar). **No es un release estable** - se publica como prerelease para no interferir con el comprobador de actualizaciones de la build normal.

## Novedad principal: Quick Save / Quick Load real en juegos multi-hilo

El savestate llevaba tiempo oculto por no funcionar de forma fiable en juegos reales (crash garantizado). Se ha investigado y arreglado la causa raíz:

- Un hilo bloqueado en una espera del kernel (condvar, IPC, sleep, arbitraje de dirección) vive dentro de una fibra host cuyo verdadero punto de retorno está en su propia pila, no en el `Svc::ThreadContext` serializado. Restaurar por encima de esa memoria dejaba la fibra despertando en un mundo que ya no coincidía con lo que esperaba, y el juego se autoterminaba (`svcBreak`).
- `Restore()` ahora deja completamente intactos el contexto y la memoria de pila de cualquier hilo que siga dormido en el momento de restaurar, y solo rebobina los hilos realmente parados y la memoria compartida.
- Se corrige también el mismo bug de sincronización de caché de GPU que afectó al Lemon Cheater (`ReadBlockU

releases.name: SkyEmu v2
releases.body:
It is my pleasure today to announce the release of the SkyEmu v2 GBA/GB/GBC emulator. 

You can access the web build [here](https://web.skyemu.app/v2) or download the native builds linked at the bottom. 

Lets take a look at some of the new features in this release:

# Display Options

SkyEmu v2 adds 5 high quality upscaling shaders covering the most popular upscaling algorithms. All filters are antialiased so they look nice at a variety of resolutions and the LCD filters even adapt themselves to the characteristics of the screens of the HW being emulated. For example when playing a DMG game the LCD filter's pixel outline color changes and its sub-pixel grid is replaced with a slight drop shadow.

![SkyEmu-Shaders](https://github.com/skylersaleh/SkyEmu/assets/7118296/ab75b4af-2abe-4d69-9448-631daddc8637)

On top of the upscaling shaders SkyEmu v2 adds a bunch of scaling and display emulation options:
- Forced Integer Scaling
- Stretch to Fit Scaling
- Color Correction 
- Screen Ghosting
- Screen Rotation
- Customizable DMG GB Color Palette

Its primary focus is to provide a good user experience through a good mixture of tradeoffs of accuracy, performance, features and usability. # Features - [Highly accurate Game Boy Advance emulation](docs/Accuracy.md) - Game Boy and Game Boy Color Emulation - Experimental Nintendo DS support (only capable of running homebrew currently) - Cross Platform: Windows, MacOS, Linux, Web App (with touch screen controls for iOS and Android) - Game Controller and Rumble Support with configureable keybinds - 4x Save Slots with screenshot preview - Game fastforward and rewind support (supporting [very long rewind times](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sfc_1NKbiKg)) - Support for emulating the Real Time Clock - CPU, MMIO, and Memory Debuggers - Dark and Light Themes - Support for loading official BIOSs dumps Web build: https://web.skyemu.app/v1/

releases.name: v0.2.1: All treat, no trick! 🎃
releases.body:
Hi everyone! I'm happy to announce a new release, two months after the previous one. 

Before I get to the changelog, some special notes:

- From this release onwards, the old list of supported apps is replaced by the new, crowdsourced [touchHLE app compatibility database](https://appdb.touchhle.org/).
- In case you missed it, the [touchHLE app archive](https://touchhle.org/app-archive/) was recently launched. It only has one app at the moment, but that's hopefully just the start. If you were an indie developer in the early iPhone days, please get in touch!
- If you want to get notified about future releases, you might want to join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/sVMXc8z3eS). You can't post there, but you'll be @'d with updates. There's also a [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@touchHLE) where I post short gameplay videos with new releases.
- If you want to help me keep working on this full time, please consider [supporting me financially](https://liberapay.com/hikari_no_yume).

Finally, a big thanks to all the other contributors who made this release what it was! If it weren't for them, there might not have been any new game support in this release.

Happy Hallowee

releases.name: v0.2.0: touchHLE on Android!
releases.body:
At long last, it's here: the first release to work on Android, the first release with an app picker UI, the first release with (very limited) UIKit support, and much more!

This release required a lot of effort, and not just from me! I want to especially thank @ciciplusplus, who dared to try to port touchHLE to Android and somehow succeeded. I also want to thank @KiritoDv and @LennyKappa, who also made big contributions to this release.

Thank you all for your continued patience and support. I hope you enjoy!

~ hikari

[Update 2023-09-01: When the release was tagged and uploaded yesterday, two changelog entries were mistakenly in the v0.1.2 section rather than v0.2.0. The copies of the changelog below and in the release zip files have now been corrected. Additionally, the `OPTIONS_HELP.txt` file was mistakenly absent from the Android release zip file, but it has now been added.]

releases.name: v0.1.2, the iPhone SDK 15-year anniversary release… kinda.
releases.body:
Hi everyone!

Yesterday was the 15-year anniversary of the iPhone SDK launch. Isn't that neat? I was hoping this release would be out yesterday, but alas I didn't manage to get everything done in time.

Something very cool _did_ come out yesterday, though: [_Stop Skeletons From Fighting_'s video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OF36SAm-S7o) about the touchHLE project, and the story of Super Monkey Ball for iPhone. It's pretty fantastic, please watch it!

Anyway, without further ado, here's what touchHLE v0.1.2 has to offer…

Compatibility:

- API support improvements:
  - Various small contributions. (@hikari-no-yume, @nitinseshadri)
  - Some key parts of `UIImage`, `CGImage` and `CGBitmapContext` used by Apple's `Texture2D` sample code are now implemented. Loading textures from PNG files in this way should now work. (@hikari-no-yume)
  - MP3 is now a supported audio file format in Audio Toolbox. This is done in a fairly hacky way so it might not work for some apps. (@hikari-no-yume)
- New supported apps:
  - Touch & Go LITE
  - Super Monkey Ball Lite (full version was already supported)

Quality:

- The version of stb\_image used by touchHLE has been updated. The new version inclu

Compatibility:

- API support improvements:
  - Various small contributions. (@hikari-no-yume, @nitinseshadri, @LennyKappa, @RealSupremium)
  - Basic POSIX file I/O is now supported. Previously only standard C file I/O was supported. (@hikari-no-yume)
  - Very basic use of Audio Session Services is now supported. (@nitinseshadri)
  - Very basic use of `MPMoviePlayerController` is now supported. No actual video playback is implemented. (@hikari-no-yume)
- New supported app: Crash Bandicoot Nitro Kart 3D (version 1.0 only).

Quality and performance:

- The code that limits CPU use has reworked in an attempt to more effectively balance responsiveness and energy efficiency. Frame pacing should be more consistent and slowdowns should be less frequent. No obvious impact on energy use has been observed. (@hikari-no-yume)
- The emulated CPU can now access memory via a more direct, faster path. This can dramatically improve performance and reduce CPU/energy use, in some cases by as much as 25%. (@hikari-no-yume)
- Fixed missing gamma encoding/decoding when rendering text using `UIStringDrawing`. This was making the text in _Super Monkey Ball_'s options menu look pretty ugly. (@hikari-no-yum

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.8.5 - Lock on, Gyroscope, First-person, New Settings
releases.body:
**Memory cards now work with the real game.** A save exported
from a GameCube memory card or from Dolphin loads straight into Open Nectar,
and a save made here can be taken back the other way. Around it: gyro aiming
on pads and phones, a rebuilt settings menu that explains every option, a
first-person view that finally works properly, and sixteen new gameplay
options, including Lock-On and Charge borrowed from Pikmin 3.


## Memory cards

- **Genuine GameCube saves are readable at last.** The checksum that guards
  each section of the card was reading its words in the host's byte order.
  On a PC that is the opposite of a GameCube, so every real save looked
  corrupt, the game offered to repair it, and repairing it destroyed the
  progress. The sum is now computed the way the console computes it.
- **Cards written by older builds still load.** They carry the old sum, so
  it is accepted on read and quietly rewritten correctly the next time the

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.6 - Android Release

### **_Open Nectar now runs on Android._**
Same code, same disc images, same saves format natively on your phone with touch controls designed for the game rather than a virtual GameCube pad glued on top. Alongside it, custom texture packs on every platform, a much faster renderer, and a batch of desktop fixes.

One APK, both discs USA Rev. 1 and European

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.4.7
releases.body:
**_Needs a retail disc (USA Rev 1 or Europe)._**

### **_Gameplay and controls_**

- Mouse look no longer cancels WASD. A small mouse delta was treated as stand-and-turn, so Olimar hitched while running and aiming.
- F1 can bind analog triggers and sticks, not only face buttons.
- DualSense remaps work for the stick and Circle; F1 capture no longer stores the key that opened the bind.
- F1 menu on DualSense / Linux no longer walks itself (IMU / extra motion joystick).
- Quick-release Pikmin grabs work on PC.

### **_Graphics_**

- Enemy health gauges draw again. Triangle fans were missing GXEnd on PC.
- Boss generators use the correct type on PC.

- Post-process colour writes stay enabled, so the chain does not go black.

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.4.6 - Fixes
releases.body:
### **_Tutorials_**
Olimar’s prompts no longer show @ or leftover GameCube glyphs. They print the F1 binding you are using: keyboard names on keyboard, pad names on pad. The C-Stick is T/F/G/H on the default layout. In mouse-cursor mode, A / B / Z also list Left Click, Right Click and Middle Click.

### **_Menus_** 
Leaving a stage no longer leaves depth of field on the file-select and title screens. Those screens have no HUD split, so the pass was blurring the whole interface. In the field, DoF is unchanged.

### **_Throws_**
A short tap to throw no longer vanishes while the chosen Pikmin is still grabbing or walking over. The throw waits until it is actually in hand. (#11)

### **_Post-process_** 
If the last scene draw left colour or alpha writes off, bloom and the rest of the chain could keep the previous frame. The pass now writes every channel and puts the mask back afterwards. (#12)

### **_Mods_** 
F1 → Mods → Hold to Pluck. Off by default, same tap-per-sprout as the disc. Turn it on and holding Extract after the first pluck keeps going; release or whistle stops. (#13)

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.4.6
releases.body:
A small hotfix on top of 0.4.5. Same discs, same languages, same installer.

### _**Controls**_
Remapping from F1 actually waits for the next key or button. Confirming a row with Enter, Space or A used to store that same press as the new binding, so the list flicked back to the default. It now waits until you let go, then takes the next input. Escape cancels.

On a DualSense the Gamepad list no longer walks itself, and Circle is bindable without kicking you out of the submenu. Linux was treating the pad’s motion sensor as a stick held down, and Circle was still “Back” on the frame after you bound it.

### _**PAL on Windows**_
The European build no longer dies before a window appears. It was asking which language to use during static initialisation, which on MinGW can run before C++ streams exist. USA never asked, which is why only PAL crashed. Linux was already fine.

### _Saves_
A first save with no backup slot chosen could write off the start of the card buffer and crash. Direct boot was the usual way to hit it. The title → file-select path was already safe.

**_Still the same:_** you supply your own copy of Pikmin. Supported discs: USA Rev 1 and Europe.

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.4.5 - PAL Multilanguage
releases.body:
### **_The European release_**
Open Nectar now runs the PAL disc, and that means it now runs in Spanish, French, German and Italian as well as English.

Nothing is translated by this project: the European disc ships all five languages, and the game has always known how to use them. What was missing was a port that could be built for that release at all — the game's own code is compiled here, and it is conditional on which release it came from in four hundred places.

The installer recognises which disc you gave it and installs the matching build. If the disc carries more than one language it asks which you want to play in, and every language is installed regardless, so changing your mind later is a menu row and not a reinstall. F1 → Language.

The choice is written to your settings, so it survives.

### **_Widescreen_**
The HUD no longer stretches to fill a 16:9 frame. It is drawn in a wide space with its pieces anchored where they belong — life on the left, the sun bar centred, counters and the day to the right — so the world can be genuinely wide without the interface being pulled out of shape or leaving dark bands at the sides.

And things at the edges stop disappearing. The 3D

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.4 - Graphics Mods
releases.body:
**_Graphics_**
A Graphics page in the F1 menu, with every effect switchable. The port has to keep running on modest hardware the reference machine here is a GTX 1050 so nothing on this page is mandatory, and everything applies as you move through it, against the scene behind the menu.

- Depth of field. The focus plane follows Olimar. What sits at his distance stays sharp; what is nearer or further falls away. Four steps, Off through Strong, and the sharp band is measured as a fraction of how far the camera is from him, so it behaves the same in the close follow view and the far one.

- Ambient occlusion. Contact shadows in creases, under leaves, where a Pikmin meets the ground. Computed from the depth buffer alone — the port has no G-buffer — at half resolution with a depth-aware blur.

- Bloom. Three named steps rather than a slider, because bloom looks wrong across most of the range a slider would offer.

- Antialiasing. FXAA, applied to the finished image. Deliberately not MSAA: Pikmin's undergrowth is alpha-tested quads, and MSAA does nothing for those edges because they are not geometry.

- Colour grading, with gamma, brightness and saturation.

- Fog: the game's own, which t

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.3.5 - Permadeath / Photo Mode
releases.body:
Two new mods

## Permadeath

Lose Olimar and the run is over: the day does not simply end, and the save
is erased.

It is not a setting in the F1 menu. Permadeath belongs to a save file, so
you choose it once when you create the file and the file screen marks
the files that carry it. Loading a normal file cannot put you in a run
that deletes itself, and loading a permadeath file cannot quietly turn the
rule off. Copy a permadeath file and the copy is one too.

The erase goes through the game's own delete, the same one the file
screen's Erase option calls, so a slot lost this way ends up in exactly
the state a manually deleted one does not in some state only this mod
produces.

The prompt and the mark on the file screen are built from the game's own
panes, textures and font. They are part of those screens rather than drawn
on top of them.

## Photo mode

Press **F3**. The world stops — every Pikmin, every creature, the captain,
the clock — and the camera is yours.

| | |
|---|---|
| `WASD` | move along the look direction |
| `Space` / `Ctrl` | up / down |
| Arrow keys | look |
| `Q` / `E` | tilt, `R` levels |
| `Shift` / `Alt` | faster / slower |

It flies like a first-person camera

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.3.1
releases.body:
A maintenance release on top of 0.3. Three fixes and two new mods.

## Fixed: controller sticks inverting at full travel

Reported from a controller on Windows. SDL axes run to -32768, so negating
one for the Y flip gives 32768, one past what the pad's signed byte holds,
which wraps around. Pushing the stick fully up read as fully down. The
conversion now clamps, and a test covers the ends of the range.

## Fixed: settings menu unusable with a controller

A held direction advanced the cursor once per frame, which made rows
impossible to land on. Navigation now waits 450 ms before repeating, then
repeats about four times a second.

## New mod: Pikmin limit

*F1 → Mods → Pikmin limit.* How many Pikmin may be on the field at once,
from 50 up to 999. The original is 100.

The Onion's capacity, the field roster and the renderer's matrix pool are
all sized from this number, so it takes effect when a stage loads rather
than in the middle of a day. Tested to 945 Pikmin on screen at once.

High values do cost frame rate, and how much depends on your machine,
the menu warns you.

## New mod: Day length

*F1 → Mods → Day length.* Between 5 and 30 minutes of play per in-game day,
10 being the

releases.name: Open Nectar 0.3 — Native Windows Release
releases.body:
This release brings Open Nectar to Windows. The same source now builds a native x86-64 executable for both Linux and Windows, and the mouse wheel gains two uses that make the game noticeably more comfortable to play.

**_Windows_**
Open Nectar cross-compiles from Linux to a native Windows executable with MinGW-w64. It is not an emulator and not a wrapper: the same reconstructed game code, built for Windows.

**_Mouse wheel_**
A new setting in the Mods menu chooses what the wheel does. One setting with two values rather than two switches, so the two uses can never both be active.

- Pikmin colour. The wheel picks which colour to throw next. It cycles only through colours actually in your squad: with one colour it does nothing, with two it alternates, with three it cycles. If the chosen colour is out of reach, the captain still grabs the nearest Pikmin rather than nothing.

- Camera zoom. The wheel pulls the camera between 0.45× and 2.50× of its normal distance. Returning the wheel to colour selection restores the default distance.

**_Frame rate_**
The 120 FPS mode now actually presents at 120. The port paces presentation itself rather than using the driver's VSync, and that limiter

releases.name: Open Nectar v0.2.1
releases.body:
This release makes the game audible. Open Nectar now runs Pikmin's original JAudio sound engine instead of a reimplementation, so music, sound effects and cinematic audio all play.

**_Sound_**
Earlier builds drove audio through a hand-written mixer. It reproduced parts of the engine, but instruments were detuned, some effects never fired, and several scenes were silent.

Open Nectar 0.2 runs the game's real audio code instead. The sequencer, instrument banks, oscillators and channel manager are the original ones; only the boundary where the GameCube's DSP chip used to sit is replaced by a software renderer.

**_What this fixes:_**

- Background music in menus, the save-file screen, the world map and all stages
- Sound effects: whistle, Pikmin, enemies, objects, UI
- Cinematic audio, including the ending sequence
- Instrument tuning and timbre
- Boss-mode music layers, scene transitions and pausing
- Static and dropouts
- The audio path is covered by a self-test (--audio-self-test) that walks the scenes, stages, boss transitions, muting, sound effects and cinematic streams.

**_Frame rate_**
A 120 FPS option joins 30 and 60 in the F1 settings menu. All three are safe: the game inte

This release adds a bundled driver for Snapdragon 8 Elite, brings back the audio presets that were missing from 0.6.0, fixes DLC imports and GPU hangs, lets each touch control be resized, and redesigns the launcher.

## Graphics

- **Adreno 8xx driver for Snapdragon 8 Elite.** A source-built Mesa 26.3 Turnip with a fix for the newer Qualcomm gralloc, which otherwise leaves the whole image garbled on Adreno 830. Auto selects it on SM8750 devices unless an imported driver is chosen, and it always renders with `TU_DEBUG=sysmem,nobin`. On Adreno 830 it measured about 12 ms of GPU time per frame at 100% resolution, compared with about 26 ms on the stock driver. Other Adreno 8xx GPUs can select it manually; it has only been validated on Adreno 830.
- **High refresh rate displays.** The game requests the display's fastest mode and passes the FPS option to Android, so FPS settings above 60 are no longer capped at 60 by vsync on 120 Hz phones.
- **Fewer frozen images on Adreno 6xx** ([#170](https://github.com/SansNope/UnleashedRecomp-Android/issues/170)). Some Turnip builds return early from an unlimited GPU wait; the game now waits again instead of reusing buffers the GPU is still drawing.

- Added a persisted game-storage choice for internal memory, app folders and Android/media folders on mounted volumes, including SD cards. Optional verified copying keeps the original game, mods, settings and saves (issue #90).
- Added missing translations in English, Russian, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese and Portuguese, including mod settings, updates, storage selection and localized file/installer errors.
- Fixed overlapping guest memory copies with `memmove`, addressing the ring crash and broken collision triggers (PR #158 fix by [puopg (Michael Chen)](https://github.com/puopg)).

releases.name: Unleashed Recomp Android 0.5.3
releases.body:
small update

### Vulkan driver profiles

- Added **Adreno 8xx Experimental (sysmem+flushall)** as a separate, non-default launcher choice.
- The new profile uses the bundled whitebelyash Mesa 26.2 gen8-capable driver and forces the exact `TU_DEBUG=sysmem,flushall` workaround for artifact-prone Adreno 8xx devices.

### Android audio presets

- Added an experimental **POCO F8 Ultra (low latency)** preset. It reduces the internal FIFO cushion from 16 to 8 guest audio frames (about 85 ms to 43 ms) and requests AAudio's exclusive low-latency path to avoid HyperOS selecting an approximately 80 ms shared hardware burst.
- The existing **Default** and **AYN** behavior is unchanged. The POCO-specific path is opt-in because it may crackle, stall or lose sound on devices whose AAudio/MMAP implementation is unreliable.

### Experimental Mali GPU support

- The game now runs on recent Mali GPUs through the stock system Vulkan driver — no custom driver needed. Requires a Valhall-generation GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver (e.g. Mali-G610/G615/G710/G715/G720). Confirmed working on a Dimensity 8300 Ultra (Mali-G615). - Game textures (BC1–BC5, BC7) are transcoded to ETC2/EAC on the CPU at load time on devices whose driver lacks BC support — with the same GPU memory footprint as the originals. sRGB content keeps correct sRGB sampling via the ETC2 sRGB formats.

releases.name: v2.0.0
releases.body:
## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 2.0.0

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

This is a major release for this project, where the biggest change is that we have completely redesigned the bottom screen UI to feel more native to Silksongs design language. The bottom screen UI should now feel familiar to anyone who has used the in-game menu and any action can be taken from the bottom screen menu, making the in-game menu obsolete.

Thanks to Kaz Kirigiri for doing most of the design work and providing sketches for this revamped UI!

## Changes since 1.1.0

### Completely revamped bottom screen UI

- All tabs have been revamped to follow the in-game menu as close as possible
- Every action from the menu can now be done from the bottom screen. Use items, change crest and tools, place markers
- Smoothly animated item selection, tab switching, etc

## Changes since 2.0.0-rc1

### Dual screen
  - Zoom slider on the map: drag up to zoom in, down to zoom out. Fades out like RESET when you're not touching the map
  - Equipping and unequipping tools is animated: the tool flies

releases.body:
## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 1.0.3

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

This version focuses on making the app compile on more devices. We had a major issue for many devices where it would not compile due to .NET issues. This has now been fixed. Many other fixes based on user reports too. 

We have now tested and gotten reports of the app working on:

- Ayn Thor
- Retroid Pocket Flip 2
- Ayn Odin 3
- Galaxy Fold 8
- Galaxy Fold 6 (black bars in-game, will be fixed)
- AYANEO Pocket EVO
- KONKR Pocket Fit 8e
- Google Pixel 10 (emulator)

Open an issue if your device (including the ones listed above) is not working

### Builds no longer die
- Run .NET on Android's own runtime instead of Debian's glibc
- Fixed the build process being permanently unstartable on some devices (Odin 3, Samsung, Xiaomi), and being killed mid-conversion for memory as a cached process
- Cap memory and parallelism on 4 GB devices, and retry once when reclaimed; ≥7 GB unchanged
- 16 KB page alignment, for Android 15 devices that can't map 4 KB libraries
- Cancell

releases.name: v1.0.3-rc3
releases.body:
## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 1.0.3-rc3

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

## Changes

- Fixed the build process failing to start for good — `Unknown authority` / `the activity manager would not start it`, surviving an app restart (#4)
- Build process retries now cover the ~10s the system allows, instead of giving up after 3s
- A build process killed mid-run is now reported instead of hanging the build
- When a build process still won't start, the message says to force stop — closing from recents never helped
- Cancelling a build now ends only the build process, instead of taking the launcher with it
- Fixed a failed save promoting a stale temp over the real save and reporting success, leaving an unloadable slot
- The save directory is created before each launch, and leftover temps are cleared
- The game's own faults are now captured in the log instead of only logcat

releases.name: v1.0.3-rc2
releases.body:
## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 1.0.3-rc2

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

## Changes

- **Setup no longer fails with `Unknown authority …mono`.** Each build step runs in a fresh process, and asking for the next one before the last had finished exiting could be refused — which threw away the whole build. It now waits for the previous one and retries a refusal instead of giving up.

- **The C++ conversion is much less likely to be killed part-way.** It ran at the lowest priority Android has, so on a busy device the system reclaimed it first — showing up as `il2cpp failed after …s` or a stall on "Converting to C++". It now runs at the launcher's own priority.

- **"Converting to C++" and "Retargeting content" show real progress.** Both bars sat still for the whole step, which was indistinguishable from a hang — one report gave up after 30 minutes on a build that may have been fine. They now count the files as they land.

- **View log no longer crashes**, the log is written where you can actually get at it (the app's external files folder, with a Save button),

releases.name: v1.0.2
releases.body:
## Hollow Knight: Silksong Android 1.0.2

**Note when updating from a previous version**: This will trigger the porting process again, but it is heavily cached, so should only take a few minutes.

This is a small update to the porting process, no in-game changes. This update makes folder selection the new default way of linking your manually supplied game files, this makes it way easier to select the game files. The old folder still works, so this is backwards compatible.

## Changes

- Folder picker for selecting game files (instead of putting them in a specific app-storage folder)
- Don't log Steam username in logs for privacy reasons (when sharing logs)
- Reset build and change folder buttons on "Start porting" screen to more easily restart the porting process if something goes wrong.

Escape backs out of menus. Toggle it in Remap > "Point and click menus".
- On the map, zooming out past the farthest distance or tapping the A prompt opens the world map. On touch, a two-finger twist rotates the map.
- Optional Trilogy-style pointer aim (Controls > Options > Aiming, off by default): the crosshair moves over the screen and the view turns once it nears the edge. Works with the mouse, twin stick, gyro and touch.

releases.name: v0.26.0 hotfix 2
releases.body:
Remastered beam improvements, Android touch buttons that name what they do in morph ball and menus, and a memory leak fix for visor static.

**You need your own disc image:** Metroid Prime USA (`GM8E01`, revisions 1.00, 1.01 and 1.02) or the experimental PAL release (`GM8P01`). No disc image or game assets are included.

## What changed

### Remastered
- The Power Beam, Plasma Beam and missile impacts now use Remastered's effects. The Plasma Beam's impact and charge effects give off their own light.
- Ice Beam effects keep Remastered's material and particle rotation, and the charged Plasma Beam effect follows the arm cannon's rotation.
- More menu and HUD text is translated on a USA disc with another language selected (door names, START, and strings Remastered reworded).
- These need a re-import: the port reminds you at launch; run it from F1 > Remastered.

### Android
- With button descriptions on, the touch buttons name what they do in morph ball (Bomb, Boost, P.Bomb, Spider), in the pause menu, on the map and in message boxes (#106).
- A quick upward swipe of the aim finger uses the Spring Ball (F1 > Touch controls, on by default).

### Fixes

Steadier X-ray and thermal reticles while walking, a scan lock that no longer drops when a scan finishes, and better crash logging on Android.

### Logging
- On Android 11 and later, the log now begins with how the previous run ended (killed for low memory, native crash, not responding, and so on) and how much memory it used. A crash that leaves no crash report, such as a low-memory kill, now leaves a trace in the next log.
- The log records the game's memory, the system's free memory and the GPU texture totals every 30 s, and sooner when they change sharply. On Android it also records the system's low-memory warnings.

releases.name: v0.23.0
releases.body:
Photo mode, quick resume after closing the app or a crash, skippable boot logos, save states improvements, save import and conversion between every Metroid Prime release: PAL, USA 1.01 and 1.02 discs supported by default, a 1.00 sequence-break compatibility option, button prompts that follow your rebinds, and Remastered sun shadow cascades.

**You need your own disc image:** Metroid Prime USA (`GM8E01`, revisions 1.00, 1.01 and 1.02) or the PAL release (`GM8P01`). No disc image or game assets are included.

## What changed

### New
- **Photo mode:** the pause menu's "Photo mode" row (touch works too), F8 (rebindable), F1 > Game or the console `photo`. Freezes the game with a free camera, FOV and roll, an option to show or hide Samus, and PNG capture at 1x, 2x or 4x resolution. Works during cutscenes too. On Android the panel fits the screen, an invisible stick on the left flies the camera and dragging looks around, and photos go to `Pictures/Metroid Prime`.
- **Quick resume** (F1 > Save states, on by default): the game keeps a resume state at most about 30 seconds old, written as it goes, so it survives quitting, sending the app to the background on Android, crashes and power loss.

### Controls
- **Separate menu buttons** (on by default): the pause screen, front end and map use the pad's standard A/B/X/Y, bumpers and D-pad even when gameplay buttons are remapped (#57). They have their own Remap rows ("Menus and map"); turn the option off to have menus follow gameplay bindings again.
- Port menu (F1, Back+Start), save state (F5), load state (F9) and screenshot (F12) are now ordinary bindings that Remap can show and change. The Port menu always keeps a binding.

releases.name: v0.21.0
releases.body:
Unified control remapping, smoother high-FPS presentation, faster movie decoding, and fixes for sound settings, PAL map icons and cached GLES shaders.

**You need your own disc image:** Metroid Prime USA v1.00 (`GM8E01`) or the experimental PAL release (`GM8P01`). No disc image or game assets are included.

## What changed

### Controls
- One **F1 > Controls > Remap** list for keyboard, mouse, touch and controllers, with inline editing and recording, chords, trigger modes and per-controller profiles.
- Choose the active controller beside the binding profile.
- Mouse wheel cycles owned beams by default; next/previous beam and visor actions can be remapped (#61).
- Choose on-screen button glyphs. Pads without GameCube trigger-click buttons no longer keep unusable L/R click mappings (#59).

### Fixes and improvements
- Rolling Morph Ball interpolation and stale camera motion during scan freezes fixed (#70).
- Slow front-end ticks no longer spiral into excessive catch-up work; faster, output-equivalent THP movie decoding (#54).
- Saved Mono/Stereo/Dolby Surround sound mode is preserved, with an F1 audio setting (#65).
- F1 > System can reset configuration after confirmation, backing it

releases.name: v0.20.0
releases.body:
Faster rendering, a very experimental macOS build, experimental PAL disc support, Remastered-style movement under
twin stick and mouse aim, and fixes for music after loading a save state (#52),
options lost on restart (#45), a stuck control lock after Hall of the Elders
(#44), Steam Deck trigger mappings (#53) and TLS errors connecting to
Archipelago on Windows (#51).

**You need your own disc image.** Metroid Prime (USA) v1.00, `GM8E01` disc 0
revision 0, or (experimental) the PAL release `GM8P01`. Nothing here contains
any part of the game — no disc, no assets.

## What changed

### Performance

- **Cheaper graphics command processing**: far fewer pipeline rebuilds and less
  work per draw.
- **Shaders compile on several threads at startup**, so the startup compile
  finishes several times faster.
- The Remastered room import is faster on Android.

### New

- **macOS (very experimental, needs testing)**: a first build for Apple
  Silicon Macs (arm64, macOS 13 or later). It builds and passes its tests on
  CI, but **it has never been run on a real Mac**, so rendering (Metal),
  input, audio and saves are all unverified. Expect problems, and please
  report what works and what does

releases.name: v0.18.0
releases.body:

instead of black bars (#12), ultrawide cutscenes are no longer close-ups (#14),
and Android gets touch controls you can lay out yourself plus a new twin-stick

### Screens of any shape

- **Wider than 4:3, the widescreen HUD bends instead of stretching**: the
  helmet's curves stay curved, and the bars slide out with their struts.

releases.name: v0.17.0
releases.body:
Clearer handling of incomplete disc images (#8), cutscenes and menus that fit
ultrawide screens (#9), Discord Rich Presence out of the box, and Remastered
rooms lit by their baked lightmaps, with a much faster re-import.

**You need your own disc image.** Metroid Prime (USA) v1.00, `GM8E01` disc 0
revision 0. Nothing here contains any part of the game — no disc, no assets.

## What changed

### Disc images

- **An incomplete disc image is refused instead of hanging on the Nintendo
  logo** (#8). A truncated or partly downloaded image (often a compressed
  RVZ/WIA/GCZ) used to open, then freeze the game at the logo. The port now
  checks the end of the image when it opens it and asks for another one.
- If reading the disc still fails mid-game, the port remembers it: the next
  start refuses that image, asks for another, and shows a red notice saying
  why.
- An unexpected error in the game loop is now written to the log and reported,
  instead of leaving the game frozen.

### Ultrawide screens

- **Cutscenes keep their 16:9 framing** on screens wider than 16:9 (21:9 and
  up) instead of being cropped at the top and bottom (#9).
- The file-select and other front-end screens are pilla

releases.name: v0.16.0
releases.body:
A fix for black worlds on Adreno 730 phones (#7), an OpenGL ES option,
Remastered sun shadows, more room for the touch controls, and much better
logs for reporting GPU problems.

**You need your own disc image.** Metroid Prime (USA) v1.00, `GM8E01` disc 0
revision 0. Nothing here contains any part of the game — no disc, no assets.

## What changed

### Graphics drivers

- **Adreno 730 (Galaxy Z Fold4, Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 phones): the world no
  longer draws black** (#7). The driver mishandled a bounds check in the
  shaders; on that GPU the port now uses a form it handles. Other GPUs are
  unchanged.
- **F1 > Video > Quality > *Use OpenGL ES*** renders through OpenGL ES instead
  of Vulkan, for drivers that draw wrongly under Vulkan. It takes effect after
  a restart, and if OpenGL ES crashes while starting, the next start goes back
  to Vulkan by itself.

### Diagnostics

The log (`metroid_prime_port.log`; on Android in
`Android/data/org.metroidprime.port/files/`) now carries what's needed to
debug a GPU or driver problem, so please attach it to a report:

- **Device and GPU:** phone model, chipset and Android version, the GPU's
  driver, features and limits, the screen formats it

releases.name: v0.15.0

**You need your own disc image.** Metroid Prime (USA) v1.00, `GM8E01` disc 0
revision 0. Nothing here contains any part of the game — no disc, no assets.

  again when you lift your finger.
- **Beam and visor wheels** replace the D-pad. Hold the Visor or Beam button,
  slide to a sector and let go. They show the game's own icons (read from
  your disc), with beams in their colours. Items you don't have yet are left
  empty, and letting go in the centre cancels. *Tap Visor for Scan Visor* is
  an option.
- While you hold **A** to charge a beam, sliding that finger also aims.

releases.name: v0.14.0
releases.body:
Crash fixes (Windows enemies, a memory corruption, the Remastered import on

- **SIGSEGV silencioso com ROM vazia**: quando o carregamento da ROM falhava, o fluxo continuava para `init()` com o buffer da ROM vazio e o `do_rom_read` desreferenciava ponteiro nulo (o app "simplem

APK **release assinado** (arm64-v8a), compilado pelo workflow `release` no commit `152aace` (`fix/turnip-driver-reload-on-relaunch`).

### Instalação
1. Baixe o arquivo `dk64recomp-android-v1.0.2-android-r4.apk` abaixo.
2. No Android, permita "instalar apps de fontes desconhecidas" para o seu navegador/gerenciador de arquivos.
3. Instale o APK. Não é preciso desinstalar builds anteriores assinados com esta mesma chave.

### Assinatura
- Keystore: CN=DK64 Recompiled Android (release)
- SHA-256 do APK: `f667b276b3f7bb26…`

### Requisitos
- Android 8.0+ (API 26), arm64-v8a
- ROM do Donkey Kong 64 (NTSC-U 1.0) — selecione no app na primeira execução

releases.name: v2.5: DCNet, new on-screen gamepad, DreamConn+ and DreamPicoPort adapters
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* DCNet: a free dedicated VPN service for Dreamcast games that only needs a basic Internet connection. 30 game servers are already available and more are coming.
* Improved on-screen gamepad for Android and iOS: move and resize controls, custom designs, arcade-specific layout, unused controls hidden based on game (arcade) or device (console games).
* Support for physical Dreamcast controllers with DreamConn+ and DreamPicoPort adapters: gamepad, VMU, vibration pack and more.
* New Dreamcast "Full Controller" with 2 analog axes and all possible buttons (Panther DC controller).
* Better analog axis emulation when using a keyboard or digital buttons by using a ramp up/down curve.
* Hardware CD/DVD/BD-ROM support
* GD-ROM arcade games load time reduced to zero.
* Improved GD-ROM access time, particularly with HLE BIOS.
* Fixed: Vulkan per-pixel mode on Mali GPUs.
* Work-around an OpenGLES bug in many drivers displaying the game screen upside down.
* Per-game VMU now compatible with multidisk games.
* Support for some encrypted cheats.
* Online support for Hundred Swords, PBA Bowling, StarLancer and The Next Tetris.

## Fixed Games
* D+VINE
* Doom 64
* Fur Fighters
* Ki

# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.9.0

**RISC overclocking no longer costs more than it should, and the Virtual Jaguar desktop app
ships: a standalone emulator for macOS, Windows and Linux built on the same core.**

v3.9.0 brings the RISC overclock fix and new timing work to the core, and debuts the standalone desktop app (https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/issues/833). For
RetroArch and Provenance users the change is the overclock fix, an experimental DSP timing
model behind an existing option, and measurement tooling. With default settings the core is
byte-identical to v3.8.0 in the cartridge and CD boot matrices. No option keys were removed, no
listed option values changed, and the savestate format stays v17.

---

## Core

  of each frame in a wait loop emulated twice the cycles, all of them spinning, and a 2x
  overclock ran far slower than it should. The fast-forward is exact at any clock scale, so it
  now stays on (https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/pull/891, https:

releases.name: v3.6.1
releases.body:
# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.6.1

**A patch release for one thing: booting the core with no content now lands you
in the CD BIOS, which is the screen you insert a disc from.**

v3.6.0 shipped no-content boot (#646) and the disk-control interface (#651) so
you could launch the core bare, put in a disc, and reach the Virtual Light
Machine with an audio CD. That combination did not work. This fixes it.

---

## The fix

No-content boot resolved to a **bare console**: the boot ROM running against a
zeroed cartridge window. That is authentic for a Jaguar with no CD unit
attached — and it is a dead end. The CD BIOS is what offers "insert a disc",
and it is mapped as a cartridge at `$800000`, so nothing reachable from the
empty-slot screen could ever get to it. The headline feature of v3.6.0 was
unreachable by construction.

Starting with no content now boots the **real CD BIOS**, which comes up on its
own insert-disc screen. No files are required: an external CD BIOS ROM in your
system directory is preferred if you have one, and otherwise an embedded image
is used.

Two smaller consequences of the same path, fixed alongside:

- It reported cartridge mode rather than **CD mode with an emp

# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.6.0

**Debugger & libretro surface.** A GDB remote stub you can attach a real
`m68k-elf-gdb` to, the disk-control interface that makes booting with no content
and swapping a disc mid-session possible, a user-authorable patch/hook file, and
a broad SIMD pass that speeds up the parts of the emulator that were actually
hot.

91 commits since v3.5.1.

---

## Debugging

**GDB remote serial protocol stub** (#652). Attach `m68k-elf-gdb` (or lldb) to a
running core over TCP and debug Jaguar code the way you would any other target:

- Breakpoints, single-step, register and memory access.
- The **GPU and DSP appear as GDB threads**, so you can inspect all three
  processors from one session.
- Connect scripts, editor plugins, and an installer ship in the repo; see
  `docs/gdb-stub-design.md`.

The per-instruction cost of the stub was measured, attributed per processor, and
reduced — see "Performance" below.

## libretro surface

**Disk control interface** (#651). The core now implements
`SET_DISK_CONTROL_EXT_INTERFACE`, which was the shared blocker behind two
features:

- Launch the core with **no content** and insert a disc afterwards.
- Reach the **Virtual Lig

# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.5.1 — Settings clarity

A small fast-follow to v3.5.0. No emulation behaviour changes: this release
makes the core options honest about what they do to each other, shortens the
descriptions that had grown into walls of text, and fixes a test fixture that
kept `make test` red on a clean tree.

---

## The compounding-settings warning (#595)

**DSP Idle-Loop Fast-Forward** (`virtualjaguar_risc_idle_skip`) is the largest
speed lever the core has — 66-87% less DSP interpretation on the titles
measured in #569 — and `DSPExec()` switches it off entirely while certain
other options are active. Nothing said so. A user who raised the RISC
overclock on a borderline-slow title paid the overclock's own cost *and*
silently forfeited the bigger win, which reads as "overclocking made it much
slower" with no explanation available anywhere.

```
virtualjaguar_risc_clock_scale -- the DSP idle-loop fast-forward is doing
nothing, so this combination can run slower than idle-skip alone. Your
settings are honored, not overridden.
```

releases.body:
# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.5.0 — Texture packs, controllers, and performance

Every Jaguar controller Atari shipped (and one it never did) is now emulated,
community HD texture packs can replace a title's own blitter art, the Voice
Modem can carry an actual voice, and the core can finally be profiled **on
the device** instead of only on a developer's desktop.

---

## Highlights

### Texture replacement packs (#369, #528)

Present community HD art in place of a title's own blitter tiles.

- **Texture Dump Mode** (`virtualjaguar_texture_dump`) writes every unique blitter
  source tile a title uses to `<system>/vj_texdump/<cart CRC32>/` as a PNG, for
  pack authoring. Tiles are identified by a hash of their raw source bytes only —
  the palette is advisory metadata, never identity, because the Jaguar blitter
  never sees one.
- **Texture Replace** (`virtualjaguar_texture_replace`) presents packs from
  `<system>/vj_texpacks/<cart CRC32>/<hash>.png`, and the option is shown only
  when a pack exists for the loaded title. Packs are true colour; a pack pixel
  with alpha below 128 falls through to the stock pixel instead of covering it.
- **Tier 1** (16bpp source tiles at 1x through s

releases.name: v3.4.0
releases.body:
# Virtual Jaguar v3.4.0 — Peripherals, texture dump, BIOS selection

The peripheral release. Every controller the Jaguar ever had — plus the one
that let you phone your opponent — now works, alongside a texture-dump
pipeline for HD pack authors and user-selectable boot ROMs.

## Highlights

### Ultra Vortek netplay, over the emulated Jaguar Voice Modem (#481)

The JVM was Atari's voice-and-data modem, and *Ultra Vortek* was the only
retail title that spoke to it. Both sides of that conversation now work:
the modem's command protocol is emulated on JERRY's UART, and the "phone
call" is carried over the existing netlink transport (TCP or RetroArch
netplay).

Type **911** on the numpad at the Ultra Vortek title screen, one player
dials any number, the other answers.

The protocol was reverse-engineered from the retail ROM rather than
guessed: a custom Phylon command set (not AT), 16-bit words console→modem,
3-byte replies back, and a mutual DTMF probe as the line-quality check. The
full decode is in [`docs/voice-modem.md`](docs/voice-modem.md).

Verified on two real iOS devices, not only headlessly.

releases.body:
# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.3.0

Hi-res completion and correctness release: the internal-resolution track now
adds real detail on **every** video mode and on scaled sprite objects, not just
CRY gouraud — which is what finally makes 2D titles benefit. Alongside it, a
run of root-caused game and infrastructure fixes, several of them found by
reading the original Atari/Flare TOM netlists rather than guessing.

## Highlights

- **Hi-res for RGB16 direct mode** (#382). All hi-res detail was previously
  CRY-only: every other video mode rendered at 1x and replicated rows. Measured
  across ~3,000,000 rendered scaled calls, Val d'Isère and Primal Rage are
  **100% RGB16** — so an entire class of titles was getting pure upscaling with
  zero added detail, including titles whose blits already produced supersampled
  content that was then discarded. Alien vs Predator now shows 6.9 million
  non-uniform sub-pixel blocks where it previously had none.
- **Hi-res Stage 3: OP scaled-object supersampling** (#367). Scaled bitmap
  objects (SCBITOBJ) now carry real sub-pixel content instead of box
  replication — the piece the design calls "the second real win", and the one
  that helps 2D titles r

releases.body:
# Virtual Jaguar libretro v3.2.0

Enhancement-suite release: the first two visible pieces of the modern-emulation
track (#338) — full-precision gouraud rendering and 2x internal resolution —
plus a cluster of game-fix work: Raiden's two bugs, Power Drive Rally's
mid-game sound freeze, and damaged CDI V2 rips now booting.

## Highlights

- **True Color gouraud rendering** (#341). New core option
  `virtualjaguar_true_color` renders gouraud-shaded pixels at full precision
  (chroma × 24-bit intensity) through a shadow framebuffer, removing shading
  banding in 3D titles. The game-visible 16-bit framebuffer is unchanged —
  savestates, achievements, and emulation behaviour are bit-identical.
  CRY 16bpp video modes only. Default off.
- **2x internal resolution** (#351, #353, #359). New core option
  `virtualjaguar_internal_resolution` (`1x`/`2x`, restart required) renders
  internally at a multiple of native resolution — and qualifying blits are
  supersampled with real sub-pixel content (fractional-walk source sampling,
  the "Stage 2" of the design), so 3D titles gain genuine detail; anything
  that doesn't qualify falls back to exact 2×2 box replication. The emulated
  machine cann

New-feature release: Jaguar GameDrive support, clock-scale (overclock) options,

test suite that now covers the CD path in CI with no commercial discs.

  `virtualjaguar_risc_clock_scale` 0.5x–2x) for framerate-limited titles.
  Defaults are bit-identical to previous behaviour; bus/DRAM costs stay in

# Virtual Jaguar libretro v2.3.0

and RISC performance work, hardware accuracy fixes across TOM/JERRY/DSP, and

## Highlights

- DAC resamples I2S output when SCLK changes at runtime — fixes audio pitch
  drift in games that reconfigure the sound clock.
- iOS / Provenance stability: all statics properly reset on core unload/deinit.
- Expanded test suite: 56,500+ automated assertions, framebuffer integrity
  checks, EEPROM lifecycle, audio pipeline, and timing diagnostics.

## What's new

- **AvP**: fixed alpha noise / red visual artifacts — blitter now skips

# Virtual Jaguar libretro v2.2.0

A large libretro-fork release — bumping from upstream v2.1.0.
Closes libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro#27, #85, and many sub-issues of #38.

## Highlights

- HLE BIOS that actually boots most commercial titles — no real BIOS image required.
- Save states, SRAM/EEPROM, cheat codes, and a RetroAchievements memory map.
- Audio pipeline rewrite — interleaved JERRY with the main loop, no more frame-edge dropouts.
- ~2x speedup on DSP / GPU / memory hot paths, plus a SIMD-accelerated blitter (SSE2 / NEON / scalar) with bit-exactness CI.
- Wide hardware-accuracy pass across DSP, GPU, blitter, Object Processor, TOM, JERRY, and 68K.
- Per-button retropad remapping for the Jaguar's 21-key controller (numpad included).
- Pre-built libretro cores for 14 platforms with an automated tagged-release workflow.
- Headless `make test` harness covering HLE BIOS, event queue, blitter SIMD bit-exactness, DSP MAC40, save states, and screenshot regressions.

## What's new

### Compatibility

- HLE BIOS improved — boot most commercial titles without a real
  BIOS image. Many games that previously needed the real BIOS, or
  worked-but-broken with it, now run on HLE BIOS too.

releases.name: v1.6 - Gamepad (Setup), QoL, UI
releases.body:
**KNOWN ISSUE:** Physical controllers are currently still broken in this build. Directory fixes are working. Recommended for touch-screen users only

Hey everyone, v1.6 is live.

I got a hold of an Android device to test with, which brought a lot of bugs to my immediate attention. I’ve done some work cleaning up the codebase to make this actually usable on devices like the Retroid, Thor, Ayaneo.

Just to be transparent: Since I'm working with Zep on the official iOS release, the Android version is going to remain an unofficial side project. However, I still want it to be a quality experience for those of you using it, so I'm pushing these QoL updates to get it stable.

**The Big Fixes:**

**Android Storage Fixed:** Closed issue #18. The directory picker now actually works. You can point it to your external SD card or any ROM folder, and it won't crash or fail to import. It respects your folder structure and keeps the app data separate.

**Immersive Mode:** Closed issue #19. The Android navigation bar now hides correctly, giving you full-screen real estate for the games. There's also a setting to remove the virtual controls completely for a true full screen mode.

**UI Overhaul:** A

releases.name: v1.5 - Cross-Platform, Multi-Carts
releases.body:
[[IMPORTANT]] Android has been sunsetted until further notice. see [the future of pocket8.](https://www.reddit.com/r/Pocket8/comments/1rerp4t/the_future_of_pocket8_important/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button) One of my biggest updates so far. Pocket8 is now officially running on Android! **New Features:** - **Android Support:** There was a huge demand for this. I'm listening! I don't have an Android device to test on currently, so please leave feedback. - **Multicart Support:** .p8.png Multi-Cart titles are now supported. **Note: .p8 Multi-Cart titles are not.** The current engine is a web-build, and does not usually support .p8 files or multicart titles at all. However, games that use absolute file names when loading carts in their code work fine. An example of a working multicart game is [Golf Monday](https://johanpeitz.itch.io/golf-monday). - **Library Management:** You can now rename and favorite your carts. Long-press to organize your collection.

**Coming Soon:** - *

releases.name: v1.4.1
releases.body:
Dpad corrections and optimizations.

- Fixed cardinal directions being difficult to input. Diagonals were too easy, this has been eased.
- Asymmetric ergonomics - up-left diagonal is easier to hit, its area has been widened to support natural motion of the thumb.
- "Finger Rolling' support added, as to push the face buttons without having to lift first. Suggested by u/Ruvalolowa.
- Auto-save on pause/exit
- blurs on buttons weren't on their own GPU layers, this has been fixed for a big performance increase.
- input mapping was creating massive garbage, this has been fixed.
- implemented silent-buffer to keep the iOS audio thread awake, greatly improving audio latency

Enjoy!

releases.name: v1.4.2

- autosave every 10 minutes, added multiple manual saves support
- more ui polish

releases.name: v1.4 - Explores tons of free PICO-8 games directly in-app!
releases.body:
v1.4 adds native BBS Explorer, making it easy to discover and enjoy thousands of community-made indie games for free.

Features:

- Infinite Discovery: Scroll through the "Featured" and "New" sections of the Lexaloffle BBS without ever leaving the app.
-  One-Tap Library: Found a masterpiece? Download it straight to your personal library to play offline anytime.

Dev Note:
I was initially holding off on this, as I thought I would need zep's permission to use SPLORE and browse PICO-8 cartridges. The method I'm using, though, lets me wrap up web-scraping into a native-like experience, essentially acting as a simple browser on your phone. No need to take proprietary software, yay!

- Critical Fix: D-Pad no longer gets stuck! (Celeste is now playable).

- Added "Swap X/O" toggle in Settings. Suggested by [u/MaxOsirus](https://www.reddit.com/r/pico8/comments/1pvf4ji/comment/nvvpo7n/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button)

- Added AltStore/SideStore Source support. Sideloaded app will auto-update when new builds come out!

releases.name: Pocket8 v1.2 - Hotfix
releases.body:
Grinding small bug fixes I notice while Christmas is still hot.

This update focuses on game feel  and precision.

### Precision Control Overhaul
* **Input Hysteresis:** Implemented a dual-threshold system for the D-pad. Inputs are now sticky and wont unpress from a thumb slip.
* **True 8-Way Support:** Switched to axis-independent logic. You can now reliably hold diagonals for tight movement.
* **Deadzone Tuning:** Optimized the deadzone (10px) to prevent jitter.

### UI Polish
* **"Jiggle Mode":** can now **Long-Press** any cartridge to enter "Wiggle Mode" for deletion, matching native iOS behavior.
* **Library Sorting:** Fixed the "Recently Played" sort order. Games now correctly bump to the top of the list when launched.
* **Visual Feedback:** The virtual controller now visually highlights multiple directions simultaneously to match your input state.

### Installation
Download `pocket8.ipa` below and install via **AltStore**, **SideStore**, or **Sideloadly**.

Merry Christmas again everyone!

releases.name: GameNative-Mali 1.2.1-mali.11
releases.body:
GameNative for Mali handhelds, rebased on upstream GameNative 1.2.1.

**Proof of concept, released as is. No support:** I do not answer bug reports or questions, and I do not take requests for devices I do not own.

Download `gamenative-mali-modern.apk` below and install it. It installs next to the stock GameNative app (package `app.gamenative.mali`). It is debug-signed with this repository's fixed key, so it upgrades over earlier `mali` builds signed with the same key.

## What changed

- **Custom driver support for PanVK on Mali.** Import a Mesa PanVK package for your device in **Driver Manager**, then select it for a game under **Graphics**. No PanVK build is bundled, and the default stays the system driver.
- A Mali device no longer lists Turnip or Qualcomm drivers, and a container that names one falls back to the system driver.
- Rebased on upstream GameNative 1.2.1.

PanVK packages for the devices I own:
[Retroid Pocket 4 Pro](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-rp4pro),
[Anbernic RG556](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-rg556),
[GameForce Ace](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-ace).

## Tested on

This exact APK is installed on my Game
